title: Chapter 36 — The Spouse Delay & The Absent Decision-Maker
intro: The objection that is usually true — prevention, the kitchen-table kit, and closing the household.

sections.title: Respect First
sections.content:
'I need to check with my spouse' is an authority objection, not a delay tactic. Treat it as legitimate every time — even when you suspect it is a dodge.

'Of course — this is a decision for your household. Let me make it as easy as possible for that conversation to happen.'

sections.title: Build the Bridge
sections.content:
Create a shareable summary. Include the product model, key features they responded to during discovery, the price, the promotion deadline, and your contact info. Make it easy for the absent partner to say yes without needing to visit the store.

'Would it help if your partner called or texted me directly with any questions? I am happy to answer anything — sometimes it is easier than relaying it secondhand.'

sections.title: Schedule the Follow-Up
sections.content:
'When do you think you will have a chance to talk about it? Would it be okay if I checked in on [specific day] to see if any questions came up?'

Get a specific day and time. A follow-up without a date is a follow-up that never happens.

If both partners are present, address both. Watch who reacts to which features. The person who does not speak often has the stronger opinion. Ask them directly: 'What is most important to you in this appliance?'

Never pressure them to decide without the partner. Never imply the partner does not need to be involved.
